data.name: Maram
data.gender_notes: Maram is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'mar' meaning desire or aspiration. The name Maram carries the meaning “Desire, aspiration” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Maram usually hope their child will grow to embody desire, aspiration and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Maram signifies the pursuit of divine knowledge and nearness to God.
data.etymology: Maram belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Desire, aspiration.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maram total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: مرام
in_arabic.meaning: المراد أو المقصود، شيء مرغوب فيه
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي، و يعني المراد أو المقصود، شيء مرغوب فيه، يدل على طموح وهدف يسعى الشخص لتحقيقه. وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الفجر: 'أَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقٍ أَمِ السَّمَاوَاتِ بَنَاهُنَّ رَبُّهُنَّ بِالْحَقِّ وَأَتَانَاهُ الْهَفَواتِ وَالشَّمسَ وَالْقَمَرَ مُحَصَّنَاتٍ فِي الْفَلَكِ يَسْعَونَ إِلَى مَرامٍ لَّن يَبلُغنَ مَرامَهم فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُمَا أَتَكَذِبَانِ

in_urdu.name: مرام
in_urdu.meaning: مراد یا مقصود، خواہش مند چیز
in_urdu.long_meaning: عربی मूल کا ایک علم مؤنث نام، مراد یا مقصود، خواہش مند چیز، یہ شخص کے مقصد یا خواہش کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ اسلامی تقویم میں اس نام کی اہمیت اس کے عربی معنی سے جڑی ہوئی ہے، جو قرآن مجید میں بھی ذکر کی گئی ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मराम
in_hindi.long_meaning: यह एक स्त्रीलिंग नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है, इच्छा या उद्देश्य, वांछित चीज़, यह नाम व्यक्ति के लक्ष्य या आकांक्षा को दर्शाता है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इस नाम का महत्व इसकी आध्यात्मिक और सांस्कृतिक पृष्ठभूमि से जुड़ा हुआ है।

in_pashto.name: مرام
in_pashto.meaning: غرض یا موخه، هیله مند شی
in_pashto.long_meaning: د عربي اصلي يو علم مؤنث نوم، غرض یا موخه، هیله مند شی، دا نوم د شخص د هدف یا هیله ښيي. په افغان او پښتون دود کې دا نوم د خپل عربي معنی سره تړلی اهمیت لري.

in_english.name: Maram
in_english.meaning: Desire, goal, or something one wishes for
in_english.long_meaning: Maram is a feminine given name of Arabic origin, meaning 'desire, goal, or something one wishes for'. It is derived from the Arabic root 'M-R-M' which is also found in the Quran. The name signifies a person's ambition or aspiration. Historically, it has been used in various Muslim cultures, symbolizing the importance of having goals and desires in life.

data.cultural_impact: The name Maram holds significant cultural importance in Islamic traditions. It carries a meaning that resonates with the values of aspiration, innovation, and determination, especially for young girls and children. Maram is strongly associated with the journey towards knowledge, both worldly and spiritual, and inspires individuals to pursue their dreams with unwavering resolve. This is significant as education and intellectual growth are highly emphasized pillars of Islamic teachings.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name Maram has strong spiritual connotations in the Islamic faith. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is said to have named Marwan ibn Al-Hakam 'Abu Maram' as a sign of his sincerity and dedication to the preservation of Islamic values and teachings. furthermore, the term Maram also holds significant meaning in Sufism, a mystical path within Islam, where it refers to a spiritual guide, a trusted path, or the 'Guiding Light' towards Allah. Such is the profound impact of the name Maram, making it a meaningful and powerful choice for individuals seeking to connect with their faith's traditions and values.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Maram bint Al-Hanafiyya (614-661 AD) was a prominent female scholar of the early Islamic period. The name Maram carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Maram was a female scholar and teacher during the time of the Prophet Muhammad and the early Islamic period. She was a member of the Hanafi school of thought and is considered one of the earliest female scholars in Islamic history.

trends: revival of interest in early Islamic women scholars
modern_usage.modern_context: Maram is a name that has seen a resurgence in popularity in modern times, particularly among those interested in the history of early Islamic women scholars. Her legacy as a prominent female scholar and teacher during the time of the Prophet Muhammad and the early Islamic period continues to be studied and celebrated.
